verify.title: Verify the inverter limit
verify.intro: SunCore lowers the inverter limit once, for about a minute, and watches what the export does. That shows whether the value limits the export at the grid point or the inverter's AC output. Afterwards your own limit comes back.
verify.intro_assisted: Set the inverter limit to assisted mode first. You confirm the one write; SunCore proposes nothing else meanwhile.
verify.intro_import: The test limit always leaves the house load, the battery charging and a margin: it cannot cause grid import.
verify.intro_abort: Closing this dialog, the emergency stop, a lost connection or a rising house load end the test at once and restore your limit.
verify.checking: Waiting for steady sunshine: {done} of {of} s.
verify.ready: SunCore proposes to lower the limit from {baseline} to {limit}. Nothing is written until you confirm.
verify.observing: The limit of {limit} is written. SunCore watches whether the export follows.
verify.releasing: Your own limit is being restored and read back.
verify.passed_export: Passed: the value limits the export at the grid point. The limit is verified now.
verify.passed_ac: Passed: the value limits the inverter's AC output. The limit is verified now.
verify.failed: The test did not pass. Your own limit is back; SunCore keeps the inverter capped at assisted mode.
verify.aborted_text: The test was stopped. Your own limit is back.
verify.status_verified: Verified: SunCore may run the inverter limit in automatic mode.
verify.status_unverified: Not verified yet: SunCore proposes inverter limits at most (assisted mode).
verify.last_failed: Last test at {at} did not pass: {reason}

p6.devices.title: Grid protection per device
p6.devices.intro: How each device behaves when the grid connection is limited.
p6.para14a.label: Controllable consumer under §14a EnWG
p6.para14a.hint: For a wallbox, heat pump or air conditioner above 4.2 kW that your grid operator may dim. While the operator asks for a reduction, SunCore keeps this device within the §14a limit and does not charge the battery from the grid. Set up the signal in the grid step.
p6.shed_rank.label: Switch-off order (shed rank)
p6.shed_rank.hint: A whole number from {min, number} to {max, number}. When the import limit, the monthly peak or backup power requires it, the lowest number is switched off first. Empty: the least important device goes first.
p6.saved: Saved. The new values apply from the next control cycle.
p6.island.title: Devices kept during backup power
p6.island.intro: When the grid fails, SunCore switches off controlled devices to protect the battery. Devices on this list stay as they are.
p6.island.legend: Devices that keep running on backup power
p6.island.hint: Keep only what really needs power in a blackout: SunCore never switches these off in island operation, so battery and inverter must carry them.
p6.island.no_backup: Backup power is not set up. Choose the backup state entity in the grid step first.
p6.mqtt.title: MQTT broker
p6.mqtt.intro: SunCore shows its entities through an MQTT broker. The Mosquitto app is found automatically; enter your own broker only if you use another one.
p6.mqtt.host_hint: Name or IP address without scheme or port, for example 192.168.1.5.
p6.mqtt.port_hint: {min, number} to {max, number}; usually 1883, with TLS 8883.
p6.mqtt.password_stored: A password is stored and never shown. Leave the field empty to keep it, or type a new one.
